figures.caption: FIG. 1. Network dynamics after 10 h of STDP-driven self-organisation. Top: Mean population firing rate; after a brief transient the network stabilises into a stationary asynchronous-irregular regime. Bottom: Spike raster of the final second (excitatory: blue; inhibitory: orange), confirming the AI state [27].

FIG. 2. Excitatory synaptic weight distributions. Top: Full distribution after 10 h of STDP, showing pronounced bimodality with peaks at w≈ 0 and w=Wmax=10 mV. Bottom: Initial (uniform) vs. final (bimodal) distributions, illustrating selective potentiation and depression driven by delay-matched STDP competition.

FIG. 4. Statistical characterisation of the 1 545 unique PNGs detected in the N=1,000 ER network. (a) Cascade-length distribution; heavy-tailed, maximum 32 spikes. (b) Group-duration distribution; modal range 20–30 ms. (c) Layer-depth distribution; most PNGs span 3–5 sequential causal layers. (d) Excitatory/inhibitory composition; near-total excitatory dominance. (e) Cascade length vs. duration scatter; approximately linear scaling expected from the fixed delay range [1,20]ms.
